title: Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale | A fairer way to talk to yourself

qcReview.basis: English PhenX Toolkit 180901 wording and order, 10 items, four agreement options, one 0–30 sum after reversing items 3, 5, 8, 9 and 10. The platform presents the options from Strongly Disagree to Strongly Agree. University of Maryland confirms public-domain status with scholarly attribution. No reference scale or local validation is claimed.

interpretations.headline: Try the voice you would use with a friend
interpretations.summary:
After giving a presentation, Alex remembers a stumble and thinks, “I made a mess of everything.” A friend who was there remembers the clear example Alex gave halfway through. Both details belong to the same afternoon. Self-esteem is the wider attitude we take toward ourselves when success and mistakes are both in view. It shows up in whether we can give ourselves a fair hearing on a difficult day.

This score combines ten answers about that general attitude. A higher total reflects a more positive view of yourself in this set of answers. The number alone cannot tell you what shaped that view. What makes the report useful is asking a question you can answer. What detail did I leave out when I told myself the story of that day?

guidance.text: Write the first sentence that came to mind after a recent setback. Under it, write two observable details. Recall something that was difficult and then something you did that helped, however small.
Turn the two details into one sentence you could say to a friend in the same position. Try keeping that sentence for the next time the original judgment returns.

If self-critical thoughts keep disrupting everyday life, consider telling someone you trust or a qualified professional what the difficult moments are like. Your score is not a prerequisite for asking for support.

limitations: Rosenberg, M. (1989). Society and the Adolescent Self-Image (rev. ed.). Wesleyan University Press. English ordering and the four-point scoring key follow PhenX Toolkit protocol 180901 (https://www.phenxtoolkit.org/protocols/view/180901).
The University of Maryland Department of Sociology lists the scale as public domain. The platform keeps its existing adult self-report eligibility.
All 10 answers are needed for the local score. This report uses the total alone, with no percentile, categorical cutoff, or separate strengths and weaknesses inferred from individual answers.
report.disclaimer: Use this adult self-report for reflection. The score describes a set of answers at one sitting and cannot determine personal worth, make a diagnosis, or support a selection decision.
